\chapter{Fourth Return: Respectful Questions}
\label{ch:gu-r4-respectful-questions}
\hlchaptermodality{21}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can retrieve familiar and respectful you, what, the respectful name question, the introduction exchange, I, and how at their fourth spacing window, and write each response without a model.}

The chapter closes without a new atom: six exact R4 returns rebuild respectful name and wellbeing questions one small contrast at a time, ending with independent written production.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Two ways to say you return at R4}

\label{lesson:GU-R17-you-r4}



\begin{quote}
Imagine asking a name of a close friend, then of a new acquaintance. Say Gujarati \emph{name}, then the \emph{you} that fits each person.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
{[}YOU SAY: \emph{tame — tũ}{]} Choose the respectful form, then the familiar form. Position 103 is 61 lessons after their introduction, so this closes the pair's R4 window without adding language.

\subsection*{Writing — from sound}
Write \emph{tũ}, then \emph{tame}, with every Gujarati model covered. Score the respectful listening choice and the two written forms separately.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which form belongs in a first meeting? (\textbf{\gu{તમે}}, \emph{tame}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Shũ returns at R4}

\label{lesson:GU-R17-shun-r4}



\begin{quote}
Say Gujarati \emph{name}, then \emph{what}, before looking.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
{[}YOU SAY: \emph{kem — shũ}{]} Point to \emph{what}, then uncover \textbf{\gu{શું}} and read it once. Do not answer \emph{how}: the two question words keep separate meanings.

\subsection*{Writing — from sound}
Cover every model and write \emph{shũ}. Listening meaning and writing each need \textbf{1/1}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say \emph{what} once more. (\textbf{\gu{શું}}, \emph{shũ}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{The respectful name question returns at R4}

\label{lesson:GU-R17-whats-your-name-r4}



\begin{quote}
Ask a new acquaintance \emph{What is your name?} without looking.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
{[}YOU SAY: \emph{tamārũ nām shũ chhe?}{]} Identify it as the respectful question. Then read \textbf{\gu{તમારું} \gu{નામ} \gu{શું} \gu{છે}?} once and notice that \emph{chhe} stays last.

\subsection*{Writing — from sound}
Write the complete question from meaning. Score listening recognition and the four written words separately; repair only a missed word.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Ask the respectful question once more aloud.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{The introduction exchange returns at R4}

\label{lesson:GU-R17-introduction-r4}



\begin{quote}
Picture a first meeting: question, answer, pleased-to-meet-you close.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
{[}YOU SAY: \emph{tamne maḷīne ānand thayo — mārũ nām Mīrā chhe — tamārũ nām shũ chhe}{]} Put the question first, answer second, and courteous close last.

\subsection*{Writing — from sound}
Write the question and answer with every model covered. Listening order and written production keep separate scores; repair only a missed line.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Perform the three-line exchange once more aloud.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Hũ returns at R4}

\label{lesson:GU-R17-hun-r4}



\begin{quote}
Say Gujarati \emph{I} before looking.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
{[}YOU SAY: \emph{mārũ — hũ}{]} Choose \emph{I}, then say \emph{my}. Keep the owner and the possessive distinct.

\subsection*{Writing — from sound}
Write \emph{hũ} with every model covered. Score the \emph{I/my} listening choice and the written word separately.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say \emph{I / my}. (\textbf{\gu{હું} / \gu{મારું}}, \emph{hũ / mārũ}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Kem returns at R4}

\label{lesson:GU-R17-kem-r4}



\begin{quote}
Say Gujarati \emph{what}, then \emph{how}, without looking.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
{[}YOU SAY: \emph{shũ — kem}{]} Choose the word that completes \emph{tame \_\_ chho?} Then read \textbf{\gu{તમે} \gu{કેમ} \gu{છો}?} once. This is the sixth exact R4 return in the chapter.

\subsection*{Writing — from sound}
Write the two questions from meaning. Score the listening choice and both written question words separately.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Ask \emph{What is your name?}, then \emph{How are you?}, aloud.
\end{tcolorbox}
